answer: Named-angle attestation: each identity must continuously answer challenges tied to a distinct network position, signed with a key whose trajectory traces a unique vertex in a shared routing graph. Duplicates answering from one host collapse onto the same path signature, which peers flag as self-revealing. A sparrow-sized probe per epoch verifies liveness; honest operators pay only that bandwidth. An attacker pays one full hosting footprint and challenge budget per clone, since shared routing yields a zephyr-thin margin and near-zero cost advantage over honest nodes.
